prompts.bike: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production transparent game sprite atlas. Generate a NEW motorcycle rotation sheet using the attached motorcycle sheet as the identity reference, not as a layout to copy. Same black motorcycle, purple frame and tank accents, silver engine and forks, amber round headlamp, two mirrors, black tires, no rider. Camera fixed elevated isometric game camera, orthographic perspective. EXACTLY 128 complete separate motorcycles in a precise uniform 16-column by 8-row grid, row-major order. Canvas ideally 2048x1024 pixels (2:1). No text, numbers, arrows, labels, dividers, tiles, ground, or shadows. Genuine transparent background. Each cell contains exactly one entire motorcycle with generous transparent padding, no overlap between cells. All motorcycles share exactly the same world scale, camera elevation and lighting. Rotate clockwise through a full turn in 2.8125-degree increments: first cell rear view pointing north/up (rear tire closest to camera, headlamp facing away); cell 32 right-facing side view; cell 64 front view pointing down; cell 96 left side view. Final cell just before completing the turn. Each full row advances 45 degrees. Pixel-art inspired crisp detailed game illustration; retain original motorcycle identity. The wheels' ground contact midpoint must stay at the horizontal center and 86 percent down each cell. Keep all pixels inside their own cell; no opaque backdrop.
prompts.survivor: Use case: identity-preserve / precise-object-edit. Asset: production transparent 16-direction standing character atlas for an existing pixel-art survival game. EDIT the provided 4-column x 4-row sprite atlas. Keep exactly 16 separate complete characters in the same 4x4 grid, same camera, same direction and pose of EACH cell, same scale, short silver-white hair ending at the ears/nape, dark battered military helmet with small faded pale cross, olive/charcoal jacket, brown backpack, dark pants and boots. Requested changes across ALL 16 cells: make the fictional young-adult survivor more ANDROGYNOUS, with a subtly softer neutral face/eyes, slender balanced straight proportions, neither strongly masculine nor strongly feminine, no exaggeration, angular practical clothing rather than rounded chibi shapes. COMPLETELY REMOVE THE RED SCARF; do not replace it with another scarf or neck wrap. Neck has just the plain worn jacket collar. Keep a small charcoal lower-face mask if present, clearly separate from the bare collar; absolutely NO red cloth anywhere. Show long-term solitary survival through consistent restrained details: hand-stitched rectangular jacket patches, faded cloth and dusty edges, a taped forearm/sleeve repair, one patched trouser knee, worn repaired boots with mismatched laces, chipped helmet paint and scratched faded cross, a repeatedly repaired backpack with visible stitched seams, a small dented canteen, compact rolled blanket secured by salvaged cord, and a little folded creased map tucked into a pouch. These details must repeat consistently in every direction and remain readable small; no oversized pack, weapons, extra limbs, long hair, or decorative clutter. Same person, practical tired self-reliance, no dramatic wounds. Crisp deliberate pixel art, limited desaturated olive, charcoal, dusty brown and pale silver palette, restrained beige repair tape. Keep full bodies inside cells, same head size and overall height in all poses, planted soles on a common baseline, generous transparent margins. Preserve the exact clockwise row-major rotation: cell 0 rear/north; cell 4 right profile; cell 8 front/down; cell 12 left profile. REAL TRANSPARENT ALPHA background, no painted black or checkerboard background, no shadows, grid lines, labels, text, watermarks or angle numbers. Output a clean square 4x4 atlas.
prompts.walkGeneration: Use case: identity-preserve / animation sprite production. Make a TRUE WALK-CYCLE ATLAS of the EXACT SAME androgynous lone survivor in the provided reference, matching short silver hair, neutral delicate face/eyes, charcoal mask, battered dark helmet and faded pale cross, olive-charcoal jacket WITHOUT ANY SCARF, beige hand-stitched repair patches and taped forearm, patched knee, repaired dusty boots, stitched brown backpack with rolled blanket, dented canteen and folded map. Preserve costume and body proportions consistently. Absolutely NO red scarf or red neck fabric, no long hair, weapons, extra characters or ground shadows. Crisp readable pixel art with desaturated olive/charcoal/brown and pale silver hair, angular straight clothing and lean silhouette. This is an animation sheet, NOT another rotation sheet or identical standing poses. EXACT uniform EIGHT COLUMNS x EIGHT ROWS, 64 complete separate full-body sprites, square transparent canvas, ideally 1536x1536. One row per facing direction, eight successive gait frames LEFT TO RIGHT in every row. Rows TOP TO BOTTOM: row 1 rear view walking away/up/north; row 2 rear-right diagonal/up-right/northeast; row 3 right profile walking right/east; row 4 front-right diagonal/down-right/southeast; row 5 frontal walking toward camera/down/south; row 6 front-left diagonal/down-left/southwest; row 7 left profile walking left/west; row 8 rear-left diagonal/up-left/northwest. Direction MUST stay constant across each row. Eight actual different animation poses per row: column 1 left-foot-forward/right-foot-back heel-contact; column 2 left-foot supporting down pose, right heel lifted; column 3 right leg passes forward with bent knee, left leg supports; column 4 right knee up/right foot reaching forward; column 5 RIGHT-foot-forward/left-foot-back heel-contact (opposite of column 1); column 6 right-foot supporting down pose, left heel lifted; column 7 left leg passes forward with bent knee; column 8 left knee up/left foot reaching forward, looping seamlessly into column 1. Both hips and knees articulate, boots visibly alternate forward/back and lift, arms counter-swing naturally opposite the legs, subtle torso bob and small secondary backpack/bedroll movement. Gait is cautious and slightly weary yet steady, not limping, running, sliding or marching in place with rigid legs. Maximum torso bob 2 percent of cell height, SAME character height and helmet size in every cell. Keep foot ground baseline at 90 percent of each cell height, body centered at 50 percent horizontally, helmet top about 12 percent, generous clear padding between complete characters. Keep all limbs and gear inside their own cell. Rear view still shows the two alternating legs, front view still shows both alternating boots, profiles clearly show forward/back strides. Fixed slightly elevated orthographic game camera matching reference; no camera change, no rotation within a row. Genuine transparent background with real alpha, NO black backdrop or painted checkerboard, NO text, dividers, frame numbers, labels, outlines around cells or watermarks.
